sentences.text: Shri Siddharth Datt - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Mohan Sausarkar - Government Advocate for the resp
Heard on I.A. No.9587/2025, fifth application under Section 430 Bnss/389(1) of Cr.P.C. for
suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the appellant.

Appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 450 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and fine of Rs.1,000/- and Section 376(3) of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 20 years and fine of Rs.1,000/- respectively, with default stipulations and Section 3A read with Section 4 of POCSO Act, 2012 (no separate sentence or fine amount has been passed).

His earlier applications were dismissed as withdrawn vide orders dated 21.08.2020, 24.03.2021,
13.07.2022 and 03.11.2022.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the trial Court has wrongly convicted and sentenced the appellant.
The age of the prosecutrix was between 15 to 16 years at the time of the incident and there were no signs of injury on the body of the prosecutrix.
Appellant has no previous criminal history.
The appellant has already undergone about 07 years of actual incarceration.
This appeal is of the year 2020 and there is no possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
Appellant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by the directions and conditions, which may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, it is prayed that the 2 CRA-183-2020 application for suspension of sentence may be allowed.
Learned counsel for the State on the other hand has opposed the application for suspension of sentence and supported the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
After perusal of the record and medical reports, it seems that the victim's hymen was found old torn.
There is no sign of other injury on the body of the victim, therefore, we are of the opinion that the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant can be considered.
Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the aforesaid I.A. is allowed.
